<!-- ============ HERO ============ -->
<header class="hero" id="hero">
<h1>Cross-Family Solver Consensus as a Gold-Free Faithfulness Metric for NL-to-FOL Translation</h1>
<p class="author">Anonymous &middot; A Preliminary Study</p>

<div class="tldr">
<p>
Translating natural language into first-order logic is useful for formal verification and reasoning, but checking
whether a formula actually captures a sentence's meaning normally requires a gold-standard reference. Gold references
are expensive and often wrong: audits find roughly 40% of annotations in standard benchmarks contain errors.
This paper tests a gold-free alternative. Several independent LLM families translate the same sentence, and an
SMT solver checks whether the candidate formula agrees with the majority. On a development dataset of 2,686
labelled items, this consensus metric achieved stratified AUROC 0.742, beating the best cheap LLM judge
by +0.099. Three peer families are enough for 97% of the signal. Confirmation on fresh data failed across
every test cell, and the metric has a fundamental rename vulnerability: a 76.5% false-alarm rate when
predicate names are changed.
</p>
</div>

<div class="hero-links">
  <a href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic@main/paper.pdf">Read the paper (PDF)</a>
  <a href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic@main/report.pdf">Read the full research report</a>
  <a href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic">Code repository</a>
</div>
</header>


<!-- ============ CONTRIBUTIONS ============ -->
<section id="contributions">
<h2>Contributions</h2>

<div class="cards">

<div class="card">
<h3>Head-to-head meta-evaluation</h3>
<p>Cross-family solver consensus tested against API judges and a 28-feature baseline stack on
NL-to-FOL faithfulness prediction. The consensus score outperforms the best cheap judge on development data
and adds signal beyond all baselines combined.</p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<h3>Mechanistic decomposition</h3>
<p>The consensus signal decomposes into endorsement (peers that agree with wrong formulas) and divergence
(peers that disagree with correct ones). Errors scatter across equivalence classes while correct translations
cluster, but this pattern degrades with sentence length.</p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<h3>Negative results on fresh data</h3>
<p>The confirmation attempt produced no testable positive cell in the long-sentence stratum. The one testable
stratum (short deterministic sentences) showed no advantage over a local judge. Every pre-registered criterion
returned not testable or unfavourable.</p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<h3>Rename tradeoff documented</h3>
<p>A 76.5% false-alarm rate under nonce predicate renames, which no variant eliminated without
sacrificing error recall. The tradeoff is structural: any vocabulary bridge that lowers divergence
also raises error endorsement.</p>
</div>

</div>
</section>


<!-- ============ METHOD ============ -->
<section id="method">
<h2>Method</h2>

<div class="prose">
<h3>Consensus scoring</h3>
<p>
Given a sentence <var>s</var> and a candidate FOL formula <var>c</var>, the method
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-1/experiment-1">[code]</a>
collects peer translations from <var>k</var> independent LLM families (Gemini, Claude, GPT, Llama, Qwen, Phi, Mistral),
each using the same few-shot prompt but a different base model.
The score is <code>c_score_align = 1 &minus; (1/k) &sum; equiv(c, p<sub>i</sub>)</code>,
where <code>equiv</code> checks logical equivalence via the Z3 SMT solver after aligning predicate names.
Higher scores mean greater divergence from the peer pool, and thus higher predicted error probability.
</p>

<h3>Predicate alignment</h3>
<p>
Independent translators choose different predicate names for the same concept
(e.g. <code>Runs(x)</code> vs. <code>IsRunner(x)</code>).
Before checking equivalence, predicates are aligned using a cost function that combines three signals:
</p>
<ol class="method-steps">
<li><strong>Structural cost.</strong> Polarity profile, argument-count match, and nesting depth.</li>
<li><strong>Text-anchor cost.</strong> Overlap between predicate-name words and source-sentence tokens, using Porter stemming and WordNet synonyms.</li>
<li><strong>Semantic signature.</strong> Truth-value profiles over random finite interpretations.</li>
</ol>
<p>
The cheapest bijections (within equal arity for predicates, separately for constants) are evaluated, and the
pair is declared equivalent if any bijection yields a Z3-verified equivalence.
</p>

<h3>Variants</h3>
<p>
Four variants are evaluated alongside the primary <code>c_score_align</code>:
<strong>c_exact</strong> (no alignment, exact-match equivalence only),
<strong>c_nf</strong> (name-free alignment by structural and semantic signatures, ignoring text anchoring),
<strong>g_score</strong> (graded, decomposes the candidate into claim units and scores the fraction unsupported by peers),
and <strong>p_peer_text</strong>
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-2/experiment-5">[code]</a>
(logistic fusion of consensus features with text-side features including bag-of-words coverage and Z3 structural match).
</p>

<h3>Evaluation framework</h3>
<p>
The development dataset contains 8,507 rows from 700 sentences drawn from the MALLS corpus and ProverQA.
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-1/experiment-3">[code]</a>
Each sentence was translated by 9 LLM families. Labels come from a three-person expert panel (adjudicated as
ERROR or CORRECT). The primary evaluation population (R_AB, both panellists agree) contains 2,686 items
(1,822 ERROR / 864 CORRECT, 292 sentences) with complexity strata for long sentences, exception clauses,
and short controls. The primary metric is stratified AUROC: items are paired only within the same source
stratum, eliminating confounds from stratum-level base rates. Confidence intervals use sentence-cluster
percentile bootstrap (B = 2,000).
</p>
</div>
</section>


<!-- ============ RESULTS ============ -->
<section id="results">
<h2>Results</h2>

<div class="prose">

<h3>Development set comparison</h3>
<p>
All metrics were evaluated on the same development population.
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-3/experiment-6">[code]</a>
The table below reports stratified AUROC with bootstrap confidence intervals.
Baselines
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-1/experiment-4">[code]</a>
include API judges (disguised and original), local judges, round-trip NLI, self-consistency,
and cross-validated feature stacks.
</p>
</div>

<div class="table-wrap">
<table>
<caption>Table 1. Stratified AUROC on development set E (R_AB, n = 2,686). Higher is better.</caption>
<thead>
<tr><th>Metric</th><th class="numeric">Strat AUROC [95% CI]</th><th class="numeric">$/item</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>c_score_align</td><td class="numeric">0.741 [0.705, 0.775]</td><td class="numeric">1.21e-4</td></tr>
<tr><td>p_peer_text (fused)</td><td class="numeric">0.753 [0.720, 0.784]</td><td class="numeric">1.21e-4</td></tr>
<tr><td>g_score (graded)</td><td class="numeric">0.694 [0.653, 0.730]</td><td class="numeric">&mdash;</td></tr>
<tr><td>c_nf (name-free)</td><td class="numeric">0.686 [0.647, 0.720]</td><td class="numeric">&mdash;</td></tr>
<tr class="group-sep"><td>c_exact (no alignment)</td><td class="numeric">0.694 [0.653, 0.730]</td><td class="numeric">&mdash;</td></tr>
<tr><td>flash-lite judge (disg.)</td><td class="numeric">0.642 [0.607, 0.676]</td><td class="numeric">4.88e-5</td></tr>
<tr><td>flash-lite judge (orig.)</td><td class="numeric">0.623 [0.593, 0.651]</td><td class="numeric">4.88e-5</td></tr>
<tr><td>nano judge (disg.)</td><td class="numeric">0.644 [0.609, 0.680]</td><td class="numeric">2.01e-5</td></tr>
<tr class="group-sep"><td>local judge Qwen-8B (disg.)</td><td class="numeric">0.674 [0.646, 0.703]</td><td class="numeric">&mdash;</td></tr>
<tr><td>round-trip NLI (min)</td><td class="numeric">0.606 [0.569, 0.645]</td><td class="numeric">2.75e-5</td></tr>
<tr class="group-sep"><td>self-consistency (5-sample)</td><td class="numeric">0.598 [0.559, 0.637]</td><td class="numeric">6.65e-5</td></tr>
<tr><td>28-feature stack</td><td class="numeric">0.735 [0.699, 0.766]</td><td class="numeric">&mdash;</td></tr>
<tr><td>28-feature stack + c_score_align</td><td class="numeric">0.774 [0.743, 0.802]</td><td class="numeric">&mdash;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

<div class="prose">

<div class="result-row">
<div class="result-cell">
  <div class="big-num">+0.099</div>
  <div class="big-label">Consensus vs. best cheap judge<br>[+0.049, +0.146] on full R_AB</div>
</div>
<div class="result-cell">
  <div class="big-num">+0.116</div>
  <div class="big-label">Consensus advantage on<br>long-sentence pool [+0.070, +0.163]</div>
</div>
<div class="result-cell">
  <div class="big-num">+0.039</div>
  <div class="big-label">Signal added to 28-feature stack<br>[+0.021, +0.057], p<sub>95</sub> = 0.009</div>
</div>
</div>

<p>
On the 284-row subsample scored by the frontier judge (Gemini 3.1 Pro), c_score_align achieves 95.7%
of the frontier judge's AUROC (ratio 0.957 [0.887, 1.034]) at 30&times; lower cost per item.
Adding consensus to the frontier judge improves AUROC by +0.037 [+0.008, +0.066].
</p>

<p>
The consensus metric achieves Kendall &tau;<sub>b</sub> = 0.692 [+0.513, +0.795] between system mean
score and R_AB error rate across 13 system&times;variant configurations. On the vocabulary-exact
subset (where candidate and gold share the same predicates), consensus still outperforms the judge
(&Delta; = +0.306 [+0.232, +0.376]), ruling out the possibility that the advantage depends on
vocabulary differences between good and bad candidates.
</p>

<h3>Mechanism</h3>
<p>
The consensus signal
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-3/evaluation-2">[code]</a>
decomposes into two components: <strong>endorsement</strong> <var>e</var> (fraction of ERROR items
endorsed by the peer majority) and <strong>divergence</strong> <var>d</var> (fraction of CORRECT items
that diverge from peers). The scatter index (ratio of pairwise disagreement among correct vs. error
items per sentence) is 4.45 [3.57, 5.77]: error translations are far more diverse than correct ones.
</p>

<p>
The net consensus degradation from short to long sentences is &Delta;(e+d) = +0.356 [+0.198, +0.493],
driven almost entirely by divergence (&Delta;d = +0.608, &Delta;e = &minus;0.252). Correct
translations of long sentences increasingly disagree with peers because independent models make
different structural choices for complex quantifier scopes and exception clauses.
</p>

<p>
Three peer families suffice for 97% of the full-pool AUROC (k<sub>95</sub> = 3), but the
long-sentence tercile requires k<sub>95</sub> = 5.
</p>
</div>

<div class="table-wrap">
<table>
<caption>Table 2. AUROC by number of peer families on development set E.</caption>
<thead>
<tr><th class="numeric"><var>k</var></th><th class="numeric">AUROC (overall)</th><th class="numeric">AUROC (long, T3)</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td class="numeric">1</td><td class="numeric">0.685</td><td class="numeric">0.581</td></tr>
<tr><td class="numeric">3</td><td class="numeric">0.757</td><td class="numeric">0.651</td></tr>
<tr><td class="numeric">5</td><td class="numeric">0.776</td><td class="numeric">0.698</td></tr>
<tr><td class="numeric">7</td><td class="numeric">0.784</td><td class="numeric">0.726</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

<div class="prose">

<h3>Confirmation attempt</h3>
<p>
The development results cannot confirm the metric's value because the development set was used to
design the scoring pipeline. Two independent test sets were constructed.
</p>
<p>
<strong>E2-A</strong>
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-4/dataset-4">[code]</a>
(550 fresh sentences) was budget-stopped before enough correct items accumulated. On the one testable stratum
(DT, short sentences from ProverQA), consensus achieves stratified AUROC 0.916, tying the local judge
(&Delta; = +0.003 [&minus;0.042, +0.052]). On L25 sentences (&ge;25 words), c_score_align falls to
0.443 (below chance), with only 42 items.
</p>
<p>
<strong>R_COMP FREE</strong>
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-3/experiment-7">[code]</a>
(long composed sentences with independent vocabulary
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-5/experiment-13">[code]</a>)
required a gloss gate for confirmatory labels. This gate failed twice (balanced accuracy 0.776 and 0.561,
below the 0.90 threshold), producing zero confirmed CORRECT rows. Under provisional non-confirmatory labels,
c_score_align achieves within-template AUROC 0.801 [0.770, 0.834] vs. the disguised judge's
0.584 [0.550, 0.618] (&Delta; = 0.217 [0.175, 0.260]).
</p>
</div>

<div class="table-wrap">
<table>
<caption>Table 3. Confirmation results. DT = short deterministic sentences; L25 = sentences &ge;25 words.</caption>
<thead>
<tr><th>Dataset</th><th>Cell</th><th class="numeric"><var>n</var> (E/C)</th><th class="numeric">AUROC</th><th>Status</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>E2-A</td><td>DT</td><td class="numeric">179 (74/105)</td><td class="numeric">0.916</td><td>Ties local judge</td></tr>
<tr><td>E2-A</td><td>L25</td><td class="numeric">42 (35/7)</td><td class="numeric">0.443</td><td>Unfavourable</td></tr>
<tr><td>E2-A</td><td>LONG</td><td class="numeric">94 (76/18)</td><td class="numeric">0.603</td><td>Not testable</td></tr>
<tr><td>R_COMP</td><td>FREE (prov.)</td><td class="numeric">1706 (602/1104)</td><td class="numeric">0.801</td><td>Non-confirmatory</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

<div class="prose">
<h3>The rename tradeoff</h3>
<p>
The predicate aligner
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-3/experiment-8">[code]</a>
introduces a fundamental false-alarm vulnerability. When correct formulas are copied with
meaning-preserving predicate renames, the consensus score should not change. In practice, the
false-alarm rate is high.
</p>
</div>

<div class="table-wrap">
<table>
<caption>Table 4. False-alarm rates on meaning-preserving renames of CORRECT candidates. NONCE = random nonsense names; SYN = WordNet synonyms. Flip = FA induced by the rename alone.</caption>
<thead>
<tr><th>Metric</th><th class="numeric">NONCE FA</th><th class="numeric">NONCE flip</th><th class="numeric">SYN FA</th><th class="numeric">SYN flip</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>c_align</td><td class="numeric">0.765</td><td class="numeric">0.605</td><td class="numeric">0.565</td><td class="numeric">0.313</td></tr>
<tr><td>c_nf (name-free)</td><td class="numeric">0.132</td><td class="numeric">0.000</td><td class="numeric">0.201</td><td class="numeric">0.000</td></tr>
<tr><td>p_peer_text</td><td class="numeric">1.000</td><td class="numeric">0.821</td><td class="numeric">0.216</td><td class="numeric">0.080</td></tr>
<tr><td>judge (disg.)</td><td class="numeric">0.229</td><td class="numeric">0.134</td><td class="numeric">0.085</td><td class="numeric">0.058</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

<div class="prose">
<p>
The name-free variant c_nf eliminates rename sensitivity (flip = 0) but at the cost of blindness to
meaning-rename errors (within-base AUROC 0.499, chance level) and lower overall discrimination (strat
AUROC 0.686 vs. 0.741). Every vocabulary bridge that lowers divergence <var>d</var> also raises
endorsement <var>e</var>: the aligner lowers <var>d</var> from 0.583 to 0.328 but raises
meaning-rename endorsement from 0.104 to 0.624.
</p>

<h3>Dead ends</h3>
<p>
Several alternatives were investigated and abandoned: a fused structural-feature filter (false-alarm
gate failure); name-free consensus c_nf (rename-invariant but blind to meaning-rename errors);
a decomposed solver-based semantic reader (balanced accuracy 0.476); LLM adjudication of disputed
items (balanced accuracy 0.662 on expert-labelled items); and candidate-signature consensus
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-4/experiment-9">[code]</a>,
which scored candidates by cueing peers with the candidate's own predicate symbols (provisional
negative: error endorsement rose to 0.459 because peers were anchored into reproducing the
candidate's errors).
</p>
</div>

</section>

<!-- ============ LIMITATIONS ============ -->
<section id="limitations">
<h2>Limitations</h2>

<ol class="limitations-list">
<li><strong>Development data only.</strong> Every positive result reported above is on data used to design the metric. The confirmation attempt produced no testable positive cell.</li>
<li><strong>Rename vulnerability.</strong> A 76.5% false-alarm rate on nonce renames means the metric will systematically penalise any translation that uses non-standard predicate names, even if semantically correct.</li>
<li><strong>Length degradation.</strong> Consensus discrimination degrades with sentence length (NET +0.356), driven by correct-translation divergence. The metric is weakest on the longest, most complex sentences, precisely the cases where gold-free evaluation is most needed.</li>
<li><strong>Label dependence.</strong> All development results depend on a three-person panel whose agreement is imperfect. The metric's advantage could partly reflect alignment with panel biases rather than with ground-truth faithfulness.</li>
<li><strong>Cost.</strong> While cheaper than a frontier judge, the consensus metric requires generating <var>k</var> peer translations per sentence, costing $0.95 per 1,000 sentences at k = 3.</li>
<li><strong>Domain.</strong> All results are on English-to-FOL from MALLS and ProverQA sources. Generalisation to other logic formalisms, languages, or sentence distributions is untested.</li>
</ol>
</section>


<!-- ============ CODE ARTIFACTS ============ -->
<section id="code-artifacts" class="code-list">
<h2>Code Artifacts</h2>

          setActive(entry.target.id);
        }
      });

    sections.forEach(function(s) { observer.observe(s); });
  }

  var lightboxImg = document.getElementById('lightbox-img');
  var lightboxCaption = document.getElementById('lightbox-caption');
  var lightboxClose = lightbox.querySelector('.lightbox-close');
  var triggerEl = null;
  var focusableInLightbox = [lightboxClose];

  function openLightbox(img) {
    triggerEl = img;
    lightboxImg.src = img.src;
    lightboxImg.alt = img.alt;
    lightboxCaption.textContent = img.getAttribute('data-caption') || '';
    lightbox.hidden = false;
    requestAnimationFrame(function() {
      lightbox.classList.add('open');
    });
    lightboxClose.focus();
    document.body.style.overflow = 'hidden';
  }

  function closeLightbox() {
    lightbox.classList.remove('open');
    document.body.style.overflow = '';
    setTimeout(function() {
      lightbox.hidden = true;
      lightboxImg.src = '';
      if (triggerEl) {
        triggerEl.focus();
        triggerEl = null;
      }
    }, 200);
  }

  lightboxClose.addEventListener('click', closeLightbox);

  lightbox.addEventListener('click', function(e) {
    if (e.target === lightbox) closeLightbox();
  });

  document.addEventListener('keydown', function(e) {
    if (!lightbox.hidden && e.key === 'Escape') {
      closeLightbox();
      e.preventDefault();
    }
    /* Focus trap */
    if (!lightbox.hidden && e.key === 'Tab') {
      e.preventDefault();
      lightboxClose.focus();
    }
  });

  /* Attach click/enter to gallery images */
  var galleryImgs = document.querySelectorAll('.fig-card img');
  galleryImgs.forEach(function(img) {
    img.addEventListener('click', function() { openLightbox(img); });
    img.addEventListener('keydown', function(e) {
      if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') {
        e.preventDefault();
        openLightbox(img);
      }
    });
  });

    });

<p>
Translating natural language into first-order logic is useful for formal verification and reasoning, but checking
whether a formula actually captures a sentence's meaning normally requires a gold-standard reference. Gold references
are expensive and often wrong: audits find roughly 40% of annotations in standard benchmarks contain errors.
This paper tests a gold-free alternative. Several independent LLM families translate the same sentence, and an
SMT solver checks whether the candidate formula agrees with the majority. On a development dataset of 2,686
labelled items, this consensus metric achieved stratified AUROC 0.742, beating the best cheap LLM judge
by +0.099. Three peer families are enough for 97% of the signal. Confirmation on fresh data failed across
every test cell, and the metric has a fundamental rename vulnerability: a 76.5% false-alarm rate when
predicate names are changed.
</p>
</div>

<!-- ============ CONTRIBUTIONS ============ -->
<section id="contributions">
<h2>Contributions</h2>

<div class="cards">

<div class="card">
<h3>Head-to-head meta-evaluation</h3>
<p>Cross-family solver consensus tested against API judges and a 28-feature baseline stack on
NL-to-FOL faithfulness prediction. The consensus score outperforms the best cheap judge on development data
and adds signal beyond all baselines combined.</p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<h3>Mechanistic decomposition</h3>
<p>The consensus signal decomposes into endorsement (peers that agree with wrong formulas) and divergence
(peers that disagree with correct ones). Errors scatter across equivalence classes while correct translations
cluster, but this pattern degrades with sentence length.</p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<h3>Negative results on fresh data</h3>
<p>The confirmation attempt produced no testable positive cell in the long-sentence stratum. The one testable
stratum (short deterministic sentences) showed no advantage over a local judge. Every pre-registered criterion
returned not testable or unfavourable.</p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<h3>Rename tradeoff documented</h3>
<p>A 76.5% false-alarm rate under nonce predicate renames, which no variant eliminated without
sacrificing error recall. The tradeoff is structural: any vocabulary bridge that lowers divergence
also raises error endorsement.</p>
</div>

</div>
</section>


<!-- ============ METHOD ============ -->
<section id="method">
<h2>Method</h2>

<div class="prose">
<h3>Consensus scoring</h3>
<p>
Given a sentence <var>s</var> and a candidate FOL formula <var>c</var>, the method
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-1/experiment-1">[code]</a>
collects peer translations from <var>k</var> independent LLM families (Gemini, Claude, GPT, Llama, Qwen, Phi, Mistral),
each using the same few-shot prompt but a different base model.
The score is <code>c_score_align = 1 &minus; (1/k) &sum; equiv(c, p<sub>i</sub>)</code>,
where <code>equiv</code> checks logical equivalence via the Z3 SMT solver after aligning predicate names.
Higher scores mean greater divergence from the peer pool, and thus higher predicted error probability.
</p>

<h3>Predicate alignment</h3>
<p>
Independent translators choose different predicate names for the same concept
(e.g. <code>Runs(x)</code> vs. <code>IsRunner(x)</code>).
Before checking equivalence, predicates are aligned using a cost function that combines three signals:
</p>
<ol class="method-steps">
<li><strong>Structural cost.</strong> Polarity profile, argument-count match, and nesting depth.</li>
<li><strong>Text-anchor cost.</strong> Overlap between predicate-name words and source-sentence tokens, using Porter stemming and WordNet synonyms.</li>
<li><strong>Semantic signature.</strong> Truth-value profiles over random finite interpretations.</li>
</ol>
<p>
The cheapest bijections (within equal arity for predicates, separately for constants) are evaluated, and the
pair is declared equivalent if any bijection yields a Z3-verified equivalence.
</p>

<h3>Variants</h3>
<p>
Four variants are evaluated alongside the primary <code>c_score_align</code>:
<strong>c_exact</strong> (no alignment, exact-match equivalence only),
<strong>c_nf</strong> (name-free alignment by structural and semantic signatures, ignoring text anchoring),
<strong>g_score</strong> (graded, decomposes the candidate into claim units and scores the fraction unsupported by peers),
and <strong>p_peer_text</strong>
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-2/experiment-5">[code]</a>
(logistic fusion of consensus features with text-side features including bag-of-words coverage and Z3 structural match).
</p>

<h3>Evaluation framework</h3>
<p>
The development dataset contains 8,507 rows from 700 sentences drawn from the MALLS corpus and ProverQA.
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-1/experiment-3">[code]</a>
Each sentence was translated by 9 LLM families. Labels come from a three-person expert panel (adjudicated as
ERROR or CORRECT). The primary evaluation population (R_AB, both panellists agree) contains 2,686 items
(1,822 ERROR / 864 CORRECT, 292 sentences) with complexity strata for long sentences, exception clauses,
and short controls. The primary metric is stratified AUROC: items are paired only within the same source
stratum, eliminating confounds from stratum-level base rates. Confidence intervals use sentence-cluster
percentile bootstrap (B = 2,000).
</p>
</div>
</section>


<!-- ============ RESULTS ============ -->
<section id="results">
<h2>Results</h2>

<div class="prose">

<h3>Development set comparison</h3>
<p>
All metrics were evaluated on the same development population.
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-3/experiment-6">[code]</a>
The table below reports stratified AUROC with bootstrap confidence intervals.
Baselines
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-1/experiment-4">[code]</a>
include API judges (disguised and original), local judges, round-trip NLI, self-consistency,
and cross-validated feature stacks.
</p>
</div>

<div class="table-wrap">
<table>
<caption>Table 1. Stratified AUROC on development set E (R_AB, n = 2,686). Higher is better.</caption>
<thead>
<tr><th>Metric</th><th class="numeric">Strat AUROC [95% CI]</th><th class="numeric">$/item</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>c_score_align</td><td class="numeric">0.741 [0.705, 0.775]</td><td class="numeric">1.21e-4</td></tr>
<tr><td>p_peer_text (fused)</td><td class="numeric">0.753 [0.720, 0.784]</td><td class="numeric">1.21e-4</td></tr>
<tr><td>g_score (graded)</td><td class="numeric">0.694 [0.653, 0.730]</td><td class="numeric">&mdash;</td></tr>
<tr><td>c_nf (name-free)</td><td class="numeric">0.686 [0.647, 0.720]</td><td class="numeric">&mdash;</td></tr>
<tr class="group-sep"><td>c_exact (no alignment)</td><td class="numeric">0.694 [0.653, 0.730]</td><td class="numeric">&mdash;</td></tr>
<tr><td>flash-lite judge (disg.)</td><td class="numeric">0.642 [0.607, 0.676]</td><td class="numeric">4.88e-5</td></tr>
<tr><td>flash-lite judge (orig.)</td><td class="numeric">0.623 [0.593, 0.651]</td><td class="numeric">4.88e-5</td></tr>
<tr><td>nano judge (disg.)</td><td class="numeric">0.644 [0.609, 0.680]</td><td class="numeric">2.01e-5</td></tr>
<tr class="group-sep"><td>local judge Qwen-8B (disg.)</td><td class="numeric">0.674 [0.646, 0.703]</td><td class="numeric">&mdash;</td></tr>
<tr><td>round-trip NLI (min)</td><td class="numeric">0.606 [0.569, 0.645]</td><td class="numeric">2.75e-5</td></tr>
<tr class="group-sep"><td>self-consistency (5-sample)</td><td class="numeric">0.598 [0.559, 0.637]</td><td class="numeric">6.65e-5</td></tr>
<tr><td>28-feature stack</td><td class="numeric">0.735 [0.699, 0.766]</td><td class="numeric">&mdash;</td></tr>
<tr><td>28-feature stack + c_score_align</td><td class="numeric">0.774 [0.743, 0.802]</td><td class="numeric">&mdash;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

<div class="prose">

<div class="result-row">
<div class="result-cell">
  <div class="big-num">+0.099</div>
  <div class="big-label">Consensus vs. best cheap judge<br>[+0.049, +0.146] on full R_AB</div>
</div>
<div class="result-cell">
  <div class="big-num">+0.116</div>
  <div class="big-label">Consensus advantage on<br>long-sentence pool [+0.070, +0.163]</div>
</div>
<div class="result-cell">
  <div class="big-num">+0.039</div>
  <div class="big-label">Signal added to 28-feature stack<br>[+0.021, +0.057], p<sub>95</sub> = 0.009</div>
</div>
</div>

<p>
On the 284-row subsample scored by the frontier judge (Gemini 3.1 Pro), c_score_align achieves 95.7%
of the frontier judge's AUROC (ratio 0.957 [0.887, 1.034]) at 30&times; lower cost per item.
Adding consensus to the frontier judge improves AUROC by +0.037 [+0.008, +0.066].
</p>

<p>
The consensus metric achieves Kendall &tau;<sub>b</sub> = 0.692 [+0.513, +0.795] between system mean
score and R_AB error rate across 13 system&times;variant configurations. On the vocabulary-exact
subset (where candidate and gold share the same predicates), consensus still outperforms the judge
(&Delta; = +0.306 [+0.232, +0.376]), ruling out the possibility that the advantage depends on
vocabulary differences between good and bad candidates.
</p>

<h3>Mechanism</h3>
<p>
The consensus signal
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-3/evaluation-2">[code]</a>
decomposes into two components: <strong>endorsement</strong> <var>e</var> (fraction of ERROR items
endorsed by the peer majority) and <strong>divergence</strong> <var>d</var> (fraction of CORRECT items
that diverge from peers). The scatter index (ratio of pairwise disagreement among correct vs. error
items per sentence) is 4.45 [3.57, 5.77]: error translations are far more diverse than correct ones.
</p>

<p>
The net consensus degradation from short to long sentences is &Delta;(e+d) = +0.356 [+0.198, +0.493],
driven almost entirely by divergence (&Delta;d = +0.608, &Delta;e = &minus;0.252). Correct
translations of long sentences increasingly disagree with peers because independent models make
different structural choices for complex quantifier scopes and exception clauses.
</p>

<p>
Three peer families suffice for 97% of the full-pool AUROC (k<sub>95</sub> = 3), but the
long-sentence tercile requires k<sub>95</sub> = 5.
</p>
</div>

<div class="table-wrap">
<table>
<caption>Table 2. AUROC by number of peer families on development set E.</caption>
<thead>
<tr><th class="numeric"><var>k</var></th><th class="numeric">AUROC (overall)</th><th class="numeric">AUROC (long, T3)</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td class="numeric">1</td><td class="numeric">0.685</td><td class="numeric">0.581</td></tr>
<tr><td class="numeric">3</td><td class="numeric">0.757</td><td class="numeric">0.651</td></tr>
<tr><td class="numeric">5</td><td class="numeric">0.776</td><td class="numeric">0.698</td></tr>
<tr><td class="numeric">7</td><td class="numeric">0.784</td><td class="numeric">0.726</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

<div class="prose">

<h3>Confirmation attempt</h3>
<p>
The development results cannot confirm the metric's value because the development set was used to
design the scoring pipeline. Two independent test sets were constructed.
</p>
<p>
<strong>E2-A</strong>
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-4/dataset-4">[code]</a>
(550 fresh sentences) was budget-stopped before enough correct items accumulated. On the one testable stratum
(DT, short sentences from ProverQA), consensus achieves stratified AUROC 0.916, tying the local judge
(&Delta; = +0.003 [&minus;0.042, +0.052]). On L25 sentences (&ge;25 words), c_score_align falls to
0.443 (below chance), with only 42 items.
</p>
<p>
<strong>R_COMP FREE</strong>
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-3/experiment-7">[code]</a>
(long composed sentences with independent vocabulary
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-5/experiment-13">[code]</a>)
required a gloss gate for confirmatory labels. This gate failed twice (balanced accuracy 0.776 and 0.561,
below the 0.90 threshold), producing zero confirmed CORRECT rows. Under provisional non-confirmatory labels,
c_score_align achieves within-template AUROC 0.801 [0.770, 0.834] vs. the disguised judge's
0.584 [0.550, 0.618] (&Delta; = 0.217 [0.175, 0.260]).
</p>
</div>

<div class="table-wrap">
<table>
<caption>Table 3. Confirmation results. DT = short deterministic sentences; L25 = sentences &ge;25 words.</caption>
<thead>
<tr><th>Dataset</th><th>Cell</th><th class="numeric"><var>n</var> (E/C)</th><th class="numeric">AUROC</th><th>Status</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>E2-A</td><td>DT</td><td class="numeric">179 (74/105)</td><td class="numeric">0.916</td><td>Ties local judge</td></tr>
<tr><td>E2-A</td><td>L25</td><td class="numeric">42 (35/7)</td><td class="numeric">0.443</td><td>Unfavourable</td></tr>
<tr><td>E2-A</td><td>LONG</td><td class="numeric">94 (76/18)</td><td class="numeric">0.603</td><td>Not testable</td></tr>
<tr><td>R_COMP</td><td>FREE (prov.)</td><td class="numeric">1706 (602/1104)</td><td class="numeric">0.801</td><td>Non-confirmatory</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

<div class="prose">
<h3>The rename tradeoff</h3>
<p>
The predicate aligner
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-3/experiment-8">[code]</a>
introduces a fundamental false-alarm vulnerability. When correct formulas are copied with
meaning-preserving predicate renames, the consensus score should not change. In practice, the
false-alarm rate is high.
</p>
</div>

<div class="table-wrap">
<table>
<caption>Table 4. False-alarm rates on meaning-preserving renames of CORRECT candidates. NONCE = random nonsense names; SYN = WordNet synonyms. Flip = FA induced by the rename alone.</caption>
<thead>
<tr><th>Metric</th><th class="numeric">NONCE FA</th><th class="numeric">NONCE flip</th><th class="numeric">SYN FA</th><th class="numeric">SYN flip</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>c_align</td><td class="numeric">0.765</td><td class="numeric">0.605</td><td class="numeric">0.565</td><td class="numeric">0.313</td></tr>
<tr><td>c_nf (name-free)</td><td class="numeric">0.132</td><td class="numeric">0.000</td><td class="numeric">0.201</td><td class="numeric">0.000</td></tr>
<tr><td>p_peer_text</td><td class="numeric">1.000</td><td class="numeric">0.821</td><td class="numeric">0.216</td><td class="numeric">0.080</td></tr>
<tr><td>judge (disg.)</td><td class="numeric">0.229</td><td class="numeric">0.134</td><td class="numeric">0.085</td><td class="numeric">0.058</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

<div class="prose">
<p>
The name-free variant c_nf eliminates rename sensitivity (flip = 0) but at the cost of blindness to
meaning-rename errors (within-base AUROC 0.499, chance level) and lower overall discrimination (strat
AUROC 0.686 vs. 0.741). Every vocabulary bridge that lowers divergence <var>d</var> also raises
endorsement <var>e</var>: the aligner lowers <var>d</var> from 0.583 to 0.328 but raises
meaning-rename endorsement from 0.104 to 0.624.
</p>

<h3>Dead ends</h3>
<p>
Several alternatives were investigated and abandoned: a fused structural-feature filter (false-alarm
gate failure); name-free consensus c_nf (rename-invariant but blind to meaning-rename errors);
a decomposed solver-based semantic reader (balanced accuracy 0.476); LLM adjudication of disputed
items (balanced accuracy 0.662 on expert-labelled items); and candidate-signature consensus
<a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-4/experiment-9">[code]</a>,
which scored candidates by cueing peers with the candidate's own predicate symbols (provisional
negative: error endorsement rose to 0.459 because peers were anchored into reproducing the
candidate's errors).
</p>
</div>

</section>

<!-- ============ LIMITATIONS ============ -->
<section id="limitations">
<h2>Limitations</h2>

<ol class="limitations-list">
<li><strong>Development data only.</strong> Every positive result reported above is on data used to design the metric. The confirmation attempt produced no testable positive cell.</li>
<li><strong>Rename vulnerability.</strong> A 76.5% false-alarm rate on nonce renames means the metric will systematically penalise any translation that uses non-standard predicate names, even if semantically correct.</li>
<li><strong>Length degradation.</strong> Consensus discrimination degrades with sentence length (NET +0.356), driven by correct-translation divergence. The metric is weakest on the longest, most complex sentences, precisely the cases where gold-free evaluation is most needed.</li>
<li><strong>Label dependence.</strong> All development results depend on a three-person panel whose agreement is imperfect. The metric's advantage could partly reflect alignment with panel biases rather than with ground-truth faithfulness.</li>
<li><strong>Cost.</strong> While cheaper than a frontier judge, the consensus metric requires generating <var>k</var> peer translations per sentence, costing $0.95 per 1,000 sentences at k = 3.</li>
<li><strong>Domain.</strong> All results are on English-to-FOL from MALLS and ProverQA sources. Generalisation to other logic formalisms, languages, or sentence distributions is untested.</li>
</ol>
</section>

============ -->\n<header class=\"hero\" id=\"hero\">\n<h1>Cross-Family Solver Consensus as a Gold-Free Faithfulness Metric for NL-to-FOL Translation</h1>\n<p class=\"author\">Anonymous &middot; A Preliminary Study</p>\n\n<div class=\"tldr\">\n<p>\nTranslating natural language into first-order logic is useful for formal verification and reasoning, but checking\nwhether a formula actually captures a sentence's meaning normally requires a gold-standard reference. Gold references\nare expensive and often wrong: audits find roughly 40% of annotations in standard benchmarks contain errors.\nThis paper tests a gold-free alternative. Several independent LLM families translate the same sentence, and an\nSMT solver checks whether the candidate formula agrees with the majority. On a development dataset of 2,686\nlabelled items, this consensus metric achieved stratified AUROC 0.742, beating the best cheap LLM judge\nby +0.099. Three peer families are enough for 97% of the signal. Confirmation on fresh data failed across\nevery test cell, and the metric has a fundamental rename vulnerability: a 76.5% false-alarm rate when\npredicate names are changed.\n</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"hero-links\">\n  <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic@main/paper.pdf\">Read the paper (PDF)</a>\n  <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic@main/report.pdf\">Read the full research report</a>\n  <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic\">Code repository</a>\n</div>\n</header>\n\n\n<!-- ============ CONTRIBUTIONS ============ -->\n<section id=\"contributions\">\n<h2>Contributions</h2>\n\n<div class=\"cards\">\n\n<div class=\"card\">\n<h3>Head-to-head meta-evaluation</h3>\n<p>Cross-family solver consensus tested against API judges and a 28-feature baseline stack on\nNL-to-FOL faithfulness prediction. The consensus score outperforms the best cheap judge on development data\nand adds signal beyond all baselines combined.</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"card\">\n<h3>Mechanistic decomposition</h3>\n<p>The consensus signal decomposes into endorsement (peers that agree with wrong formulas) and divergence\n(peers that disagree with correct ones). Errors scatter across equivalence classes while correct translations\ncluster, but this pattern degrades with sentence length.</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"card\">\n<h3>Negative results on fresh data</h3>\n<p>The confirmation attempt produced no testable positive cell in the long-sentence stratum. The one testable\nstratum (short deterministic sentences) showed no advantage over a local judge. Every pre-registered criterion\nreturned not testable or unfavourable.</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"card\">\n<h3>Rename tradeoff documented</h3>\n<p>A 76.5% false-alarm rate under nonce predicate renames, which no variant eliminated without\nsacrificing error recall. The tradeoff is structural: any vocabulary bridge that lowers divergence\nalso raises error endorsement.</p>\n</div>\n\n</div>\n</section>\n\n\n<!-- ============ METHOD ============ -->\n<section id=\"method\">\n<h2>Method</h2>\n\n<div class=\"prose\">\n<h3>Consensus scoring</h3>\n<p>\nGiven a sentence <var>s</var> and a candidate FOL formula <var>c</var>, the method\n<a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-1/experiment-1\">[code]</a>\ncollects peer translations from <var>k</var> independent LLM families (Gemini, Claude, GPT, Llama, Qwen, Phi, Mistral),\neach using the same few-shot prompt but a different base model.\nThe score is <code>c_score_align = 1 &minus; (1/k) &sum; equiv(c, p<sub>i</sub>)</code>,\nwhere <code>equiv</code> checks logical equivalence via the Z3 SMT solver after aligning predicate names.\nHigher scores mean greater divergence from the peer pool, and thus higher predicted error probability.\n</p>\n\n<h3>Predicate alignment</h3>\n<p>\nIndependent translators choose different predicate names for the same concept\n(e.g. <code>Runs(x)</code> vs. <code>IsRunner(x)</code>).\nBefore checking equivalence, predicates are aligned using a cost function that combines three signals:\n</p>\n<ol class=\"method-steps\">\n<li><strong>Structural cost.</strong> Polarity profile, argument-count match, and nesting depth.</li>\n<li><strong>Text-anchor cost.</strong> Overlap between predicate-name words and source-sentence tokens, using Porter stemming and WordNet synonyms.</li>\n<li><strong>Semantic signature.</strong> Truth-value profiles over random finite interpretations.</li>\n</ol>\n<p>\nThe cheapest bijections (within equal arity for predicates, separately for constants) are evaluated, and the\npair is declared equivalent if any bijection yields a Z3-verified equivalence.\n</p>\n\n<h3>Variants</h3>\n<p>\nFour variants are evaluated alongside the primary <code>c_score_align</code>:\n<strong>c_exact</strong> (no alignment, exact-match equivalence only),\n<strong>c_nf</strong> (name-free alignment by structural and semantic signatures, ignoring text anchoring),\n<strong>g_score</strong> (graded, decomposes the candidate into claim units and scores the fraction unsupported by peers),\nand <strong>p_peer_text</strong>\n<a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-2/experiment-5\">[code]</a>\n(logistic fusion of consensus features with text-side features including bag-of-words coverage and Z3 structural match).\n</p>\n\n<h3>Evaluation framework</h3>\n<p>\nThe development dataset contains 8,507 rows from 700 sentences drawn from the MALLS corpus and ProverQA.\n<a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-1/experiment-3\">[code]</a>\nEach sentence was translated by 9 LLM families. Labels come from a three-person expert panel (adjudicated as\nERROR or CORRECT). The primary evaluation population (R_AB, both panellists agree) contains 2,686 items\n(1,822 ERROR / 864 CORRECT, 292 sentences) with complexity strata for long sentences, exception clauses,\nand short controls. The primary metric is stratified AUROC: items are paired only within the same source\nstratum, eliminating confounds from stratum-level base rates. Confidence intervals use sentence-cluster\npercentile bootstrap (B = 2,000).\n</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n\n<!-- ============ RESULTS ============ -->\n<section id=\"results\">\n<h2>Results</h2>\n\n<div class=\"prose\">\n\n<h3>Development set comparison</h3>\n<p>\nAll metrics were evaluated on the same development population.\n<a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-3/experiment-6\">[code]</a>\nThe table below reports stratified AUROC with bootstrap confidence intervals.\nBaselines\n<a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-1/experiment-4\">[code]</a>\ninclude API judges (disguised and original), local judges, round-trip NLI, self-consistency,\nand cross-validated feature stacks.\n</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"table-wrap\">\n<table>\n<caption>Table 1. Stratified AUROC on development set E (R_AB, n = 2,686). Higher is better.</caption>\n<thead>\n<tr><th>Metric</th><th class=\"numeric\">Strat AUROC [95% CI]</th><th class=\"numeric\">$/item</th></tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr><td>c_score_align</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.741 [0.705, 0.775]</td><td class=\"numeric\">1.21e-4</td></tr>\n<tr><td>p_peer_text (fused)</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.753 [0.720, 0.784]</td><td class=\"numeric\">1.21e-4</td></tr>\n<tr><td>g_score (graded)</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.694 [0.653, 0.730]</td><td class=\"numeric\">&mdash;</td></tr>\n<tr><td>c_nf (name-free)</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.686 [0.647, 0.720]</td><td class=\"numeric\">&mdash;</td></tr>\n<tr class=\"group-sep\"><td>c_exact (no alignment)</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.694 [0.653, 0.730]</td><td class=\"numeric\">&mdash;</td></tr>\n<tr><td>flash-lite judge (disg.)</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.642 [0.607, 0.676]</td><td class=\"numeric\">4.88e-5</td></tr>\n<tr><td>flash-lite judge (orig.)</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.623 [0.593, 0.651]</td><td class=\"numeric\">4.88e-5</td></tr>\n<tr><td>nano judge (disg.)</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.644 [0.609, 0.680]</td><td class=\"numeric\">2.01e-5</td></tr>\n<tr class=\"group-sep\"><td>local judge Qwen-8B (disg.)</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.674 [0.646, 0.703]</td><td class=\"numeric\">&mdash;</td></tr>\n<tr><td>round-trip NLI (min)</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.606 [0.569, 0.645]</td><td class=\"numeric\">2.75e-5</td></tr>\n<tr class=\"group-sep\"><td>self-consistency (5-sample)</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.598 [0.559, 0.637]</td><td class=\"numeric\">6.65e-5</td></tr>\n<tr><td>28-feature stack</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.735 [0.699, 0.766]</td><td class=\"numeric\">&mdash;</td></tr>\n<tr><td>28-feature stack + c_score_align</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.774 [0.743, 0.802]</td><td class=\"numeric\">&mdash;</td></tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"prose\">\n\n<div class=\"result-row\">\n<div class=\"result-cell\">\n  <div class=\"big-num\">+0.099</div>\n  <div class=\"big-label\">Consensus vs. best cheap judge<br>[+0.049, +0.146] on full R_AB</div>\n</div>\n<div class=\"result-cell\">\n  <div class=\"big-num\">+0.116</div>\n  <div class=\"big-label\">Consensus advantage on<br>long-sentence pool [+0.070, +0.163]</div>\n</div>\n<div class=\"result-cell\">\n  <div class=\"big-num\">+0.039</div>\n  <div class=\"big-label\">Signal added to 28-feature stack<br>[+0.021, +0.057], p<sub>95</sub> = 0.009</div>\n</div>\n</div>\n\n<p>\nOn the 284-row subsample scored by the frontier judge (Gemini 3.1 Pro), c_score_align achieves 95.7%\nof the frontier judge's AUROC (ratio 0.957 [0.887, 1.034]) at 30&times; lower cost per item.\nAdding consensus to the frontier judge improves AUROC by +0.037 [+0.008, +0.066].\n</p>\n\n<p>\nThe consensus metric achieves Kendall &tau;<sub>b</sub> = 0.692 [+0.513, +0.795] between system mean\nscore and R_AB error rate across 13 system&times;variant configurations. On the vocabulary-exact\nsubset (where candidate and gold share the same predicates), consensus still outperforms the judge\n(&Delta; = +0.306 [+0.232, +0.376]), ruling out the possibility that the advantage depends on\nvocabulary differences between good and bad candidates.\n</p>\n\n<h3>Mechanism</h3>\n<p>\nThe consensus signal\n<a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-3/evaluation-2\">[code]</a>\ndecomposes into two components: <strong>endorsement</strong> <var>e</var> (fraction of ERROR items\nendorsed by the peer majority) and <strong>divergence</strong> <var>d</var> (fraction of CORRECT items\nthat diverge from peers). The scatter index (ratio of pairwise disagreement among correct vs. error\nitems per sentence) is 4.45 [3.57, 5.77]: error translations are far more diverse than correct ones.\n</p>\n\n<p>\nThe net consensus degradation from short to long sentences is &Delta;(e+d) = +0.356 [+0.198, +0.493],\ndriven almost entirely by divergence (&Delta;d = +0.608, &Delta;e = &minus;0.252). Correct\ntranslations of long sentences increasingly disagree with peers because independent models make\ndifferent structural choices for complex quantifier scopes and exception clauses.\n</p>\n\n<p>\nThree peer families suffice for 97% of the full-pool AUROC (k<sub>95</sub> = 3), but the\nlong-sentence tercile requires k<sub>95</sub> = 5.\n</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"table-wrap\">\n<table>\n<caption>Table 2. AUROC by number of peer families on development set E.</caption>\n<thead>\n<tr><th class=\"numeric\"><var>k</var></th><th class=\"numeric\">AUROC (overall)</th><th class=\"numeric\">AUROC (long, T3)</th></tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr><td class=\"numeric\">1</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.685</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.581</td></tr>\n<tr><td class=\"numeric\">3</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.757</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.651</td></tr>\n<tr><td class=\"numeric\">5</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.776</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.698</td></tr>\n<tr><td class=\"numeric\">7</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.784</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.726</td></tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"prose\">\n\n<h3>Confirmation attempt</h3>\n<p>\nThe development results cannot confirm the metric's value because the development set was used to\ndesign the scoring pipeline. Two independent test sets were constructed.\n</p>\n<p>\n<strong>E2-A</strong>\n<a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-4/dataset-4\">[code]</a>\n(550 fresh sentences) was budget-stopped before enough correct items accumulated. On the one testable stratum\n(DT, short sentences from ProverQA), consensus achieves stratified AUROC 0.916, tying the local judge\n(&Delta; = +0.003 [&minus;0.042, +0.052]). On L25 sentences (&ge;25 words), c_score_align falls to\n0.443 (below chance), with only 42 items.\n</p>\n<p>\n<strong>R_COMP FREE</strong>\n<a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-3/experiment-7\">[code]</a>\n(long composed sentences with independent vocabulary\n<a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-5/experiment-13\">[code]</a>)\nrequired a gloss gate for confirmatory labels. This gate failed twice (balanced accuracy 0.776 and 0.561,\nbelow the 0.90 threshold), producing zero confirmed CORRECT rows. Under provisional non-confirmatory labels,\nc_score_align achieves within-template AUROC 0.801 [0.770, 0.834] vs. the disguised judge's\n0.584 [0.550, 0.618] (&Delta; = 0.217 [0.175, 0.260]).\n</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"table-wrap\">\n<table>\n<caption>Table 3. Confirmation results. DT = short deterministic sentences; L25 = sentences &ge;25 words.</caption>\n<thead>\n<tr><th>Dataset</th><th>Cell</th><th class=\"numeric\"><var>n</var> (E/C)</th><th class=\"numeric\">AUROC</th><th>Status</th></tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr><td>E2-A</td><td>DT</td><td class=\"numeric\">179 (74/105)</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.916</td><td>Ties local judge</td></tr>\n<tr><td>E2-A</td><td>L25</td><td class=\"numeric\">42 (35/7)</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.443</td><td>Unfavourable</td></tr>\n<tr><td>E2-A</td><td>LONG</td><td class=\"numeric\">94 (76/18)</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.603</td><td>Not testable</td></tr>\n<tr><td>R_COMP</td><td>FREE (prov.)</td><td class=\"numeric\">1706 (602/1104)</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.801</td><td>Non-confirmatory</td></tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"prose\">\n<h3>The rename tradeoff</h3>\n<p>\nThe predicate aligner\n<a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-3/experiment-8\">[code]</a>\nintroduces a fundamental false-alarm vulnerability. When correct formulas are copied with\nmeaning-preserving predicate renames, the consensus score should not change. In practice, the\nfalse-alarm rate is high.\n</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"table-wrap\">\n<table>\n<caption>Table 4. False-alarm rates on meaning-preserving renames of CORRECT candidates. NONCE = random nonsense names; SYN = WordNet synonyms. Flip = FA induced by the rename alone.</caption>\n<thead>\n<tr><th>Metric</th><th class=\"numeric\">NONCE FA</th><th class=\"numeric\">NONCE flip</th><th class=\"numeric\">SYN FA</th><th class=\"numeric\">SYN flip</th></tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr><td>c_align</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.765</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.605</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.565</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.313</td></tr>\n<tr><td>c_nf (name-free)</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.132</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.000</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.201</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.000</td></tr>\n<tr><td>p_peer_text</td><td class=\"numeric\">1.000</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.821</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.216</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.080</td></tr>\n<tr><td>judge (disg.)</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.229</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.134</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.085</td><td class=\"numeric\">0.058</td></tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"prose\">\n<p>\nThe name-free variant c_nf eliminates rename sensitivity (flip = 0) but at the cost of blindness to\nmeaning-rename errors (within-base AUROC 0.499, chance level) and lower overall discrimination (strat\nAUROC 0.686 vs. 0.741). Every vocabulary bridge that lowers divergence <var>d</var> also raises\nendorsement <var>e</var>: the aligner lowers <var>d</var> from 0.583 to 0.328 but raises\nmeaning-rename endorsement from 0.104 to 0.624.\n</p>\n\n<h3>Dead ends</h3>\n<p>\nSeveral alternatives were investigated and abandoned: a fused structural-feature filter (false-alarm\ngate failure); name-free consensus c_nf (rename-invariant but blind to meaning-rename errors);\na decomposed solver-based semantic reader (balanced accuracy 0.476); LLM adjudication of disputed\nitems (balanced accuracy 0.662 on expert-labelled items); and candidate-signature consensus\n<a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-4/experiment-9\">[code]</a>,\nwhich scored candidates by cueing peers with the candidate's own predicate symbols (provisional\nnegative: error endorsement rose to 0.459 because peers were anchored into reproducing the\ncandidate's errors).\n</p>\n</div>\n\n</section>\n\n\n<!-- ============ FIGURE GALLERY ============ -->\n<section id=\"figures\">\n<h2>Figures</h2>\n\n<div class=\"gallery\">\n\n<figure class=\"fig-card\">\n<img\n  src=\"figures/fig_dev_auroc_v0.png\"\n  alt=\"Horizontal bar chart comparing stratified AUROC of consensus-based metrics, LLM judges, and other baselines on the development dataset. Consensus metrics (blue bars) extend further right than LLM judges (orange) and other baselines (gray), with the 28-feature stack plus consensus reaching 0.774.\"\n  tabindex=\"0\"\n  role=\"button\"\n  aria-label=\"Enlarge figure: Development Set AUROC Comparison\"\n  data-caption=\"Stratified AUROC on the development dataset for the main metrics and baselines. Error bars are 95% sentence-cluster bootstrap confidence intervals. Consensus-based metrics (blue) outperform API judges (orange) and other gold-free baselines (gray).\"\n>\n<figcaption class=\"fig-caption\">\n<strong>Figure 1. Development Set AUROC Comparison.</strong>\nStratified AUROC on the development dataset for the main metrics and baselines. Error bars are 95% sentence-cluster bootstrap confidence intervals. Consensus-based metrics (blue) outperform API judges (orange) and other gold-free baselines (gray).\n</figcaption>\n<p class=\"fig-click-hint\">Click to enlarge</p>\n</figure>\n\n<figure class=\"fig-card\">\n<img\n  src=\"figures/fig_complexity_v0.png\"\n  alt=\"Bar chart showing endorsement rate e (red) decreasing from 0.29 to 0.04 and divergence rate d (blue) increasing from 0.31 to 0.91 across short, medium, and long sentence-length terciles, with the net e+d line rising from 0.60 to 0.95.\"\n  tabindex=\"0\"\n  role=\"button\"\n  aria-label=\"Enlarge figure: Consensus Degradation with Sentence Length\"\n  data-caption=\"Decomposition of consensus error rates by sentence-length tercile. Endorsement rate e (errors incorrectly endorsed by peers) decreases with length, but divergence rate d (correct items incorrectly flagged) increases sharply, producing net degradation of +0.356 from the shortest to the longest tercile.\"\n>\n<figcaption class=\"fig-caption\">\n<strong>Figure 2. Consensus Degradation with Sentence Length.</strong>\nDecomposition of consensus error rates by sentence-length tercile. Endorsement rate <var>e</var> (errors incorrectly endorsed by peers) decreases with length, but divergence rate <var>d</var> (correct items incorrectly flagged) increases sharply, producing net degradation of +0.356 from the shortest to the longest tercile.\n</figcaption>\n<p class=\"fig-click-hint\">Click to enlarge</p>\n</figure>\n\n<figure class=\"fig-card\">\n<img\n  src=\"figures/fig_k_curve_v0.png\"\n  alt=\"Line chart with two curves showing AUROC rising steeply from k=1 to k=3 then leveling off. Three families capture 97% of the full-pool signal, but long sentences require five families to reach 95%.\"\n>\n<figcaption class=\"fig-caption\">\n<strong>Figure 3. AUROC vs. Number of Peer Families.</strong>\nStratified AUROC as a function of the number of peer families <var>k</var>, for the full development set (solid blue) and the long-sentence tercile (dashed red). Three families capture 97% of the full-pool signal, but long sentences require five families to reach 95%.\n</figcaption>\n<p class=\"fig-click-hint\">Click to enlarge</p>\n</figure>\n\n</div>\n</section>\n\n\n<!-- ============ LIMITATIONS ============ -->\n<section id=\"limitations\">\n<h2>Limitations</h2>\n\n<ol class=\"limitations-list\">\n<li><strong>Development data only.</strong> Every positive result reported above is on data used to design the metric. The confirmation attempt produced no testable positive cell.</li>\n<li><strong>Rename vulnerability.</strong> A 76.5% false-alarm rate on nonce renames means the metric will systematically penalise any translation that uses non-standard predicate names, even if semantically correct.</li>\n<li><strong>Length degradation.</strong> Consensus discrimination degrades with sentence length (NET +0.356), driven by correct-translation divergence. The metric is weakest on the longest, most complex sentences, precisely the cases where gold-free evaluation is most needed.</li>\n<li><strong>Label dependence.</strong> All development results depend on a three-person panel whose agreement is imperfect. The metric's advantage could partly reflect alignment with panel biases rather than with ground-truth faithfulness.</li>\n<li><strong>Cost.</strong> While cheaper than a frontier judge, the consensus metric requires generating <var>k</var> peer translations per sentence, costing $0.95 per 1,000 sentences at k = 3.</li>\n<li><strong>Domain.</strong> All results are on English-to-FOL from MALLS and ProverQA sources. Generalisation to other logic formalisms, languages, or sentence distributions is untested.</li>\n</ol>\n</section>\n\n\n<!-- ============ CODE ARTIFACTS ============ -->\n<section <li><a href=\"#code-artifacts\">Code</a></li>", "+</ul>", "+</nav>", "+", " <main id=\"main\">", " ", "-<!-- HERO -->", "-<header class=\"hero\" id=\"top\">", "-  <h1>Gold-Free Faithfulness Metrics for NL-to-FOL Translation</h1>", "-  <p class=\"authors\">Anonymous</p>", "-  <p class=\"tldr\">", "-    When an LLM translates a sentence into first-order logic, how do you tell whether the formula is faithful to the text without a gold reference?", "-    This paper tests a simple idea: have several independent LLM families translate the same sentence and check whether their outputs are logically equivalent.", "-    On a development dataset, this cross-family solver consensus reaches stratified AUROC 0.742, beating the best cheap LLM judge by +0.099.", "-    Confirmation on fresh data failed: every held-out cell was either not testable or unfavourable. The metric also breaks when predicate names are changed (76.5% false-alarm rate) and degrades on long sentences.", "-    These results are preliminary: the signal is real on development data, but its practical reach is not yet confirmed.", "-  </p>", "-  <div class=\"hero-links\">", "-    <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic@main/paper.pdf\">Read the paper (PDF)</a>", "-    <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic@main/report.pdf\">Read the full research report</a>", "-    <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic\">Code repository</a>", "-  </div>", "+<!-- ============ HERO ============ -->", "+<header class=\"hero\" id=\"hero\">", "+<h1>Cross-Family Solver Consensus as a Gold-Free Faithfulness Metric for NL-to-FOL Translation</h1>", "+<p class=\"author\">Anonymous &middot; A Preliminary Study</p>", "+", "+<div class=\"tldr\">", "+<p>", "+Translating natural language into first-order logic is useful for formal verification and reasoning, but checking", "+whether a formula actually captures a sentence's meaning normally requires a gold-standard reference. Gold references", "+are expensive and often wrong: audits find roughly 40% of annotations in standard benchmarks contain errors.", "+This paper tests a gold-free alternative. Several independent LLM families translate the same sentence, and an", "+SMT solver checks whether the candidate formula agrees with the majority. On a development dataset of 2,686", "+labelled items, this consensus metric achieved stratified AUROC 0.742, beating the best cheap LLM judge", "+by +0.099. Three peer families are enough for 97% of the signal. Confirmation on fresh data failed across", "+every test cell, and the metric has a fundamental rename vulnerability: a 76.5% false-alarm rate when", "+predicate names are changed.", "+</p>", "+</div>", "+", "+<div class=\"hero-links\">", "+  <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic@main/paper.pdf\">Read the paper (PDF)</a>", "+  <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic@main/report.pdf\">Read the full research report</a>", "+  <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic\">Code repository</a>", "+</div>", " </header>", " ", "-<!-- CONTRIBUTIONS -->", "+", "+<!-- ============ CONTRIBUTIONS ============ -->", " <section id=\"contributions\">", "-  <h2>Contributions</h2>", "-  <div class=\"contributions-grid\">", "-    <div class=\"contribution-card\">", "-      <h3>Cross-family consensus as a gold-free metric</h3>", "-      <p>A meta-evaluation of cross-family solver consensus as a faithfulness score for NL-to-FOL, tested head-to-head against API judges and a 28-feature baseline stack.</p>", "-    </div>", "-    <div class=\"contribution-card\">", "-      <h3>Mechanistic decomposition</h3>", "-      <p>The consensus signal decomposes into endorsement (errors recruited by the majority) and divergence (correct items that disagree). Errors scatter; correct translations cluster. This pattern degrades with sentence length.</p>", "-    </div>", "-    <div class=\"contribution-card\">", "-      <h3>Negative results on fresh data</h3>", "-      <p>The confirmation attempt on held-out data produced no testable cell in the long-sentence stratum, and the one testable stratum showed no advantage over a local judge.</p>", "-    </div>", "-    <div class=\"contribution-card\">", "-      <h3>The rename tradeoff</h3>", "-      <p>A 76.5% false-alarm rate under nonce predicate renames that no variant could eliminate without sacrificing error recall. Every vocabulary bridge that lowers divergence also raises error endorsement.</p>", "-    </div>", "-  </div>", "+<h2>Contributions</h2>", "+", "+<div class=\"cards\">", "+", "+<div class=\"card\">", "+<h3>Head-to-head meta-evaluation</h3>", "+<p>Cross-family solver consensus tested against API judges and a 28-feature baseline stack on", "+NL-to-FOL faithfulness prediction. The consensus score outperforms the best cheap judge on development data", "+and adds signal beyond all baselines combined.</p>", "+</div>", "+", "+<div class=\"card\">", "+<h3>Mechanistic decomposition</h3>", "+<p>The consensus signal decomposes into endorsement (peers that agree with wrong formulas) and divergence", "+(peers that disagree with correct ones). Errors scatter across equivalence classes while correct translations", "+cluster, but this pattern degrades with sentence length.</p>", "+</div>", "+", "+<div class=\"card\">", "+<h3>Negative results on fresh data</h3>", "+<p>The confirmation attempt produced no testable positive cell in the long-sentence stratum. The one testable", "+stratum (short deterministic sentences) showed no advantage over a local judge. Every pre-registered criterion", "+returned not testable or unfavourable.</p>", "+</div>", "+", "+<div class=\"card\">", "+<h3>Rename tradeoff documented</h3>", "+<p>A 76.5% false-alarm rate under nonce predicate renames, which no variant eliminated without", "+sacrificing error recall. The tradeoff is structural: any vocabulary bridge that lowers divergence", "+also raises error endorsement.</p>", "+</div>", "+", "+</div>", " </section>", " ", "-<!-- METHOD -->", "+", "+<!-- ============ METHOD ============ -->", " <section id=\"method\">", "-  <h2>Method</h2>", "+<h2>Method</h2>", " ", "-  <div class=\"method-step\">", "-    <h3>Consensus scoring</h3>", "-    <p>", "-      Given a sentence <var>s</var> and a candidate FOL translation <var>c</var>, collect peer translations {<var>p</var><sub>1</sub>, ..., <var>p<sub>k</sub></var>}", "-      from <var>k</var> independent LLM families (Gemini, Claude, GPT, Llama, Qwen, Phi, Mistral). Each peer uses the same few-shot prompt but a different base model.", "-      <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-1/experiment-1\">Code</a>.", "-    </p>", "-    <div class=\"formula-block\" role=\"math\" aria-label=\"c_score_align equals 1 minus 1 over k times the sum of equivalence indicators between c and each peer p_i\">", "-      c_score_align(c, s) = 1 &minus; (1/k) &sum; equiv(c, p<sub>i</sub>)", "-    </div>", "-    <p>", "-      Higher scores mean greater divergence from peers, predicting higher error probability.", "-      The <code>equiv</code> function checks logical equivalence via the Z3 SMT solver after aligning predicate names.", "-    </p>", "-  </div>", "+<div class=\"prose\">", "+<h3>Consensus scoring</h3>", "+<p>", "+Given a sentence <var>s</var> and a candidate FOL formula <var>c</var>, the method", "+<a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-1/experiment-1\">[code]</a>", "+collects peer translations from <var>k</var> independent LLM families (Gemini, Claude, GPT, Llama, Qwen, Phi, Mistral),", "+each using the same few-shot prompt but a different base model.", "+The score is <code>c_score_align = 1 &minus; (1/k) &sum; equiv(c, p<sub>i</sub>)</code>,", "+where <code>equiv</code> checks logical equivalence via the Z3 SMT solver after aligning predicate names.", "+Higher scores mean greater divergence from the peer pool, and thus higher predicted error probability.", "+</p>", " ", "-  <div class=\"method-step\">", "-    <h3>Predicate alignment</h3>", "-    <p>", "-      Independent translators choose different predicate names for the same concept (e.g., <code>Runs(x)</code> vs. <code>IsRunner(x)</code>).", "-      The aligner combines structural cost (polarity profile, argument-count match, nesting depth),", "-      text-anchor cost (overlap between predicate-name words and source-sentence tokens via Porter stemming and WordNet),", "-      and semantic signatures (truth-value profiles over random finite interpretations).", "-      The cheapest bijections are evaluated, and the pair is declared equivalent if any bijection yields a Z3-verified equivalence.", "-    </p>", "-  </div>", "+<h3>Predicate alignment</h3>", "+<p>", "+Independent translators choose different predicate names for the same concept", "+(e.g. <code>Runs(x)</code> vs. <code>IsRunner(x)</code>).", "+Before checking equivalence, predicates are aligned using a cost function that combines three signals:", "+</p>", "+<ol class=\"method-steps\">", "+<li><strong>Structural cost.</strong> Polarity profile, argument-count match, and nesting depth.</li>", "+<li><strong>Text-anchor cost.</strong> Overlap between predicate-name words and source-sentence tokens, using Porter stemming and WordNet synonyms.</li>", "+<li><strong>Semantic signature.</strong> Truth-value profiles over random finite interpretations.</li>", "+</ol>", "+<p>", "+The cheapest bijections (within equal arity for predicates, separately for constants) are evaluated, and the", "+pair is declared equivalent if any bijection yields a Z3-verified equivalence.", "+</p>", " ", "-  <div class=\"method-step\">", "-    <h3>Variants</h3>", "-    <p>", "-      <strong>c_exact</strong>: no alignment, exact-match equivalence only.", "-      <strong>c_nf</strong> (name-free): alignment by structural and semantic signatures only, ignoring text anchoring.", "-      <strong>g_score</strong> (graded): decomposes the candidate into claim units and scores the fraction unsupported by peers.", "-      <strong>p_peer_text</strong>: a logistic fusion of consensus features with text-side features (bag-of-words coverage, role accounting, Z3 structural match).", "-      <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-2/experiment-5\">Code</a>.", "-    </p>", "-  </div>", "+<h3>Variants</h3>", "+<p>", "+Four variants are evaluated alongside the primary <code>c_score_align</code>:", "+<strong>c_exact</strong> (no alignment, exact-match equivalence only),", "+<strong>c_nf</strong> (name-free alignment by structural and semantic signatures, ignoring text anchoring),", "+<strong>g_score</strong> (graded, decomposes the candidate into claim units and scores the fraction unsupported by peers),", "+and <strong>p_peer_text</strong>", "+<a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-2/experiment-5\">[code]</a>", "+(logistic fusion of consensus features with text-side features including bag-of-words coverage and Z3 structural match).", "+</p>", " ", "-  <div class=\"method-step\">", "-    <h3>Evaluation framework</h3>", "-    <p>", "-      Labels come from a three-person expert panel (adjudicated as ERROR or CORRECT).", "-      The primary evaluation metric is stratified AUROC: items are paired only within the same source stratum (sentence complexity bin), eliminating confounds from stratum-level base rates.", "-      Confidence intervals use sentence-cluster percentile bootstrap (<var>B</var> = 2,000).", "-    </p>", "-  </div>", "-", "-  <div class=\"method-step\">", "-    <h3>Development dataset</h3>", "-    <p>", "-      Dataset <var>E</var> contains 8,507 rows from 700 sentences drawn from the MALLS corpus and ProverQA.", "-      <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-1/experiment-3\">Code</a>.", "-      Each sentence was translated by 9 LLM families using a frozen few-shot prompt.", "-      The primary evaluation population (R_AB, both panellists agree) contains 2,686 items (1,822 ERROR / 864 CORRECT, 292 sentences).", "-      <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-1/experiment-4\">Baselines code</a>.", "-    </p>", "-  </div>", "+<h3>Evaluation framework</h3>", "+<p>", "+The development dataset contains 8,507 rows from 700 sentences drawn from the MALLS corpus and ProverQA.", "+<a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-1/experiment-3\">[code]</a>", "+Each sentence was translated by 9 LLM families. Labels come from a three-person expert panel (adjudicated as", "+ERROR or CORRECT). The primary evaluation population (R_AB, both panellists agree) contains 2,686 items", "+(1,822 ERROR / 864 CORRECT, 292 sentences) with complexity strata for long sentences, exception clauses,", "+and short controls. The primary metric is stratified AUROC: items are paired only within the same source", "+stratum, eliminating confounds from stratum-level base rates. Confidence intervals use sentence-cluster", "+percentile bootstrap (B = 2,000).", "+</p>", "+</div>", " </section>", " ", "-<!-- RESULTS -->", "+", "+<!-- ============ RESULTS ============ -->", " translations of long sentences increasingly disagree with their peers", "-      because independent models make different structural choices for complex quantifier scopes and exception clauses.", "- On the vocabulary-exact", "+subset (where candidate and gold share the same predicates), consensus still outperforms the judge", "+(&Delta; = +0.306 [+0.232, +0.376]), ruling out the possibility that the advantage depends on", "+vocabulary differences between good and bad candidates.", "+</p>", " ", "-  <div class=\"result-row\">", "-    <h3>Confirmation attempt: failed</h3>", "-    <p>", "-      <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-5/experiment-11\">E2-A code</a>.", "-      E2-A (fresh held-out sentences, <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/main/round-4/dataset-4\">dataset code</a>): the confirmation was budget-stopped.", "-      On the one testable stratum (DT, short ProverQA sentences), consensus achieves stratified AUROC 0.916, tying the local judge (&Delta;
